name: Noctavrel
manufacturer: Shelf labs (unlicensed); attributed to a chemist known as 'Paret'
description: Noctavrel is a Shelf-synthesized ultra-rapid sleep compound derived from a corrupted Dormacet synthesis process that produces a dramatically more potent result — full unconsciousness in 8-12 seconds, total sensory blackout, and a dreamless, near-comatose sleep state that some users describe as 'being dead.' It has no BCI compatibility layer, which is both a feature for some users and a critical risk for those with chrome-dependent autonomic systems.
effects: Unconsciousness within 8-12 seconds — faster than any licensed compound
BCI signal completely suppressed during sleep — no pings, no feeds, no surveillance
Wake state is abrupt and complete — no grogginess transition
side_effects: Dangerous with chrome above 20% body integration — can suppress chrome-regulated autonomic functions
No dream processing — REM entirely absent, emotional and memory consolidation disrupted with regular use
Abrupt unconsciousness is a physical risk if the user is not already stationary
Batch consistency varies wildly — some doses are 3x labeled potency
Documented fatalities from chrome-interaction and overdose
cultural_context: On the Shelf, Noctavrel is both practical necessity and dark legend. For people whose BCIs are hacked, surveilled, or weaponized against them, Dormacet's BCI-compatibility layer is a liability — Noctavrel's complete signal suppression means genuine privacy in unconsciousness. 'Paret,' the anonymous chemist credited with the formula, is a folk figure on the Shelf — some say she died in a batch that went wrong, others say she's still cooking. The drug's lethality with chrome is an open secret and a class marker: only people too poor for quality chrome can safely use it.
story_hooks: Someone has started distributing Noctavrel on the Shelf with a new synthesis that eliminates the chrome-interaction risk — whoever has cracked that formulation has pharmaceutical-grade knowledge and equipment that no Shelf lab should possess.

A Tier 3 investigator goes undercover on the Shelf and takes Noctavrel to avoid BCI surveillance — and wakes up 14 hours later with no memory of the middle of their sleep period, suggesting someone was in the room while they were under.

Paret is real, alive, and has approached a fixer with a request: she has a new formula that would make Noctavrel safe for everyone, but a Nightshade Pharmatech crew is hunting her for it, and she needs to disappear before she can release it.
